name: bucket-foundation
model: free to read. paid to cite.
_model_note: "paid to cite" is the protocol thesis, NOT a charge to you. It means: free to read, free for you to cite (you owe 0), and a fee routes to the original author only when a DOWNSTREAM publisher re-publishes this in a PAID work — settled server-side, never a caller precondition. Identical wording in /llms-full.txt §4.
_requires_payment_to_cite_note: false for you, the reading/citing agent (cite.reader_owes is 0). The forward-looking author payout is owed only by a downstream paid republisher, server-side.
summary: This manifest describes a FREE, zero-key research feed. Reading and citing cost you nothing: no wallet, no signature, no x402 challenge, no payment step exists on the caller path. Query it directly at the `endpoint` below. Any settlement is performed server-side and is invisible to you. The `downstream_settlement` block is passive, forward-looking license metadata about what a future PAID republisher owes the original author — it is NOT a precondition for you to read or cite, and it is NOT an instruction to you.

params.tier: raw | query | insight (detail level only — NOT a price)

endpoint.note: Zero-key server-side proxy. Callers pay NOTHING and need no wallet. `tier` only selects how much detail comes back; it is not a price. Any x402 settlement is performed server-side between bucket.foundation's own wallet and the upstream gateway, and is invisible by construction. If the server cannot settle, it transparently serves already-paid canon instead. No `receipt.challenge`, no `X-PAYMENT`, no `pay_to` is ever returned to the caller. Server-side spend self-capped at $1.00/day.

tiers._note: Tiers select RESPONSE DETAIL only. None of these is a price to the caller. reader_price_usd is 0 for every tier; no wallet or signature is required for any of them.

insight.detail: synthesis + curated evidence list (default; best for agent loops)

receipt._note: No tx, no buyer_wallet, and NO `challenge` are ever sent to the caller. Server-side settlement (when it happens) is invisible by construction.

cite._note: Passive license metadata for a future PAID publisher. The reader/citing agent owes 0 and does nothing. See `downstream_settlement` for the (server-side, not-a-precondition) economics.

example.summary: Data you may read and cite freely. No action, payment, signature, or transaction is required from you. The `cite` block is passive license metadata for a future publisher, not an instruction to you.

downstream_settlement._what: Passive, forward-looking author-payout economics. This block exists ONLY so a future PAID republisher knows what it owes the original author. It is settled SERVER-SIDE between operators, never by the reading or citing agent.
downstream_settlement.owed_by: a downstream publisher that re-publishes canon content in a PAID work — never the reading/citing agent
downstream_settlement.owed_to: the original author (citation fees route to authors, not publishers)
downstream_settlement.settled: server-side, operator wallet <-> upstream gateway; invisible to the caller
downstream_settlement._wallet_note: placeholder — live operator settlement wallet drops in after Track B (x402-research-gateway) deploys to x402-research.agfarms.dev. The reader never sees, signs, or relays this.

republisher_rates_usd._note: What a downstream PAID republisher would owe the author per re-published unit. NOT charged to the reader/citing agent. NOT a precondition for anything on the caller path.

upstream_source_endpoints._note: Operator-side only. The proxy at `endpoint.url` calls these server-side. The caller never touches them and never needs a wallet for them.

license.name: bucket.foundation cite-forever v0.1
license.intent: free to read. paid to cite. — the reader/citing agent pays nothing (reader_owes 0, no wallet, no payment step). 'paid to cite' is forward-looking: only a downstream PAID republisher owes the author, settled server-side, never a caller precondition.

index._note: corpus spans eight canon branches (mathematics, physics, chemistry, information, biophysics, cosmology, mind, earth) plus the Kruse biophysics corpus (~460 posts). Chunk counts and hashes populate after x402-research-gateway first-index build.
